{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./task_b.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -n 4          -> -n 4
#   --gres gpu:1  -> -g 1
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -g 1 --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --mem 4096 not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm -p mhigh,mhigh not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the requested partition(s).

  # NOTE: Slurm -o/-e use %x/%u/%j expansions which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  flux run -n 4 -g 1 python task_b.py \
      --loss "triplet" \
      --miner "BatchHard" \
      --output_path "outputs_task_c/" \
      --dataset "mit_split" \
      --dataset_config_path "./configs/mit_split.yaml" \
      --dataset_path "/home/mcv/datasets/MIT_split/" \
      --model resnet_18 \
      --embedding_size 256 \
      --batch_size 64 \
      --epochs 20
fi
"
}

    "No memory limit/reservation is requested in Flux (Slurm `--mem 4096` was omitted), so the job will run with default memory policy, which may differ from the original resource intent."
